definition: DeepEval is a pytest-style framework for unit-testing LLM outputs with metrics like answer relevancy, hallucination and G-Eval.
details: Created by Jeffrey Ip and Kritin Vongthongsri (Confident AI) in 2023.

explainer.lead: How to install DeepEval, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from deepeval import assert_test
from deepeval.metrics import AnswerRelevancyMetric
from deepeval.test_case import LLMTestCase

def test_answer():
    case = LLMTestCase(input="What is LoRA?",
                       actual_output="LoRA fine-tunes small low-rank adapter matrices.")
    assert_test(case, [AnswerRelevancyMetric(threshold=0.7)])
# run:  deepeval test run test_answers.py

explainer.inAi: Put LLM quality checks in CI so a prompt change that hurts answers fails the build.
explainer.jsNote: DeepEval is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is like a checklist you run after every change to a recipe, so you notice when the dish starts tasting wrong.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers write test cases for prompts and pipelines and assert on metric thresholds in CI. A pitfall is that LLM-based metrics are themselves noisy, so thresholds and evaluator models need calibration against human judgement.
tiers.paperLevel: Tests are declared like pytest cases and scored by metrics including answer relevancy, hallucination and G-Eval, with pass/fail against thresholds. Limits: metric scores are model-dependent and probabilistic, so results are not deterministic.

explainer.example: A test case feeds a question to a RAG pipeline and fails the build if answer relevancy drops below a set threshold.
